title: Embedded Canary Context Cards - Prototype Feedback & Accessibility Redlines
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Design and ship a set of small, embedded context cards for canary / canary-like rollouts in the Redwood Console. These cards surface experiment metadata (traffic split, evaluation metric summary, recent regressions), quick actions (pause, snapshot, annotate), and a lightweight CTA hierarchy intended for in-line decisioning without opening a full rollout inspector. This ticket captures the current prototype, high-level design decisions, redlines from accessibility review, and a prioritized QA/handoff checklist for engineering and PM.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype updated with final microcopy and focus order for keyboard navigation
Accessibility redlines applied: contrast, hit-targets, and readable motion settings documented
Engineering-ready component spec exported with token mapping and states (default, hover, focused, error)
PM sign-off on CTA priority and fallback behaviour for low-bandwidth/disabled telemetry
Usability test notes (n=6) and one round of microcopy adjustments incorporated
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Ortiz: Initial prototype uploaded to Figma, includes three variants (compact, expanded, and stacked). Calling out real-time metric summary as top-left element per usability recommendations.
2026-02-15 Ethan Park: Engineering feasibility check — suggested collapsing long metric names and exposing tooltip for full name; flagged animation cost for continuous live updates.
2026-02-18 Priya Nair (PM): Confirmed CTA priority: Pause > Snapshot > Annotate. For free-tier customers, pause should be disabled with documentation tooltip.

2026-02-20 Accessibility review (Sam Nguyen): Contrast for tertiary labels under WCAG AA fails at 12px; recommend increasing weight or color. Focus ring currently clipped in compact mode when stacked; needs 8px padding around interactive elements.
2026-02-24 Maya Ortiz: Applied accessibility redlines — increased label weights, adjusted color tokens, and added explicit keyboard focus order. Uploaded updated prototype and redline annotations.
2026-03-01 Design sync: Decided to throttle live metric refresh to 10s in the prototype to reduce perceived motion; fallback to last-known value when telemetry is delayed > 30s.
2026-03-04 User research: 6 participants — findings: quick actions are discoverable, but the annotate flow needed inline help; microcopy revised to add brief hint text for first-time users.

2026-03-07 QA note (Benji Ramos): Edge case — when rollout has no evaluation metrics, the card should show a single CTA 'Open full inspector' rather than empty metric placeholders. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-10 Ethan Park: Preparing engineering handoff. Requesting exported tokens and a small summary of motion easing and duration. Also asked for a trimmed list of states and a11y test checklist. Marking current status 'In Review'.
handoff_checklist: Figma file with redlines and component variants exported (tokens + CSS variables)
Prototype link with keyboard flows and motion settings captured
A11y checklist: contrast pass, keyboard order, focus targets, screenreader labels
Failure states spec: no-metrics, telemetry-delayed, offline-actions
Implementation notes: metric refresh cadence, optimistic UI behaviour for pause action
notes_for_engineering: Prefer a single reusable Card component with prop-driven slots (metric-summary, actions, annotations). Keep visual density configurable (compact vs default).
Throttle telemetry updates in UI to 10s and show 'last updated' timestamp. On telemetry timeout (>30s) surface gray placeholder and a small dismissible warning.
Pause action must be idempotent and show toast on success/failure; do not block other quick actions while pause is pending.
Add data-attribute hooks for testing and analytics: data-test-id='canary-context-card' and action-level ids.
Include CSS variables mapping to Redwood token names; annotate any new tokens in the Figma export.
Document keyboard order in handoff: Card container -> expand toggle -> first CTA (Pause) -> Snapshot -> Annotate -> close
